scopeReview: IMP-2.C.1–2: push/pull factors and intervening opportunities/obstacles across economic, environmental, cultural/social, political and demographic contexts. Distinguishes motivation, capacity, selectivity and multiple drivers without assigning legal statuses.
varietyReview: After-cost offers, intervening settlement map, travel-finance table and overlapping-motive chart; additional origin rate normalization. Applied concepts include work loss, drought/livelihood interaction, networks, permits, selective flows and amenity migration. All five skills and varied keys/difficulty.
repetitionReview: Unlike prior density/rate items, these questions use denominators to constrain driver inference. The job comparison tests secured net resources, not universal highest-wage choice; mobility constraints and overlapping survey responses supply new inferential tasks. No repeated stems or numeric-only copies.
referenceNote: Primary curriculum and IOM research/education context corroborate interacting drivers and capacity. Original synthetic scenarios/data; no institutional lesson questions, current policy claims or third-party catalog additions. No independent human review.

questions.correctOption: A leaves 300 units after costs, compared with 200 in B, despite A’s lower wage.
questions.independentReview: Independently computed remainders300/200 under secured jobs and exhaustive listed costs. No unemployment probabilities, hidden costs or universal utility model assumed; other migration motives are explicitly unmeasured.

questions.correctOption: An intervening opportunity that changes the intended destination.
questions.independentReview: Confirmed the schematic west-to-east orderOrigin15,Mid50,Far85 with a common horizontal coordinate. The behavioral change is explicitly due to suitable work at the intervening settlement, not an inferred obstacle or network.

questions.correctOption: Household B may remain because it cannot finance the fare, not because the desire to move is absent.
questions.independentReview: Checked funding gapsA1000−800=+200,B300−800=−500 under no borrowing. Held motivation equal; remaining cannot be interpreted as low concern or low desire without ignoring the stated constraint.

questions.correctOption: Several motives can overlap, so the counts do not partition the sample into exclusive groups.
questions.independentReview: Summed70+50+40=160 selections among100 respondents; because multiple responses are permitted, overlaps are necessary but exact intersections are unknown. No exclusive job-only count can be derived.

questions.correctOption: Factory closure is an origin push factor; advertised destination wages are a pull factor.
questions.independentReview: Classified by location and direction of influence, not solely by economic category. Retained conditional motivation rather than claiming that every displaced worker necessarily migrates.

questions.correctOption: Environmental stress can affect livelihoods, while resources and opportunities influence whether and where people move.
questions.independentReview: Traced drought→farm-income pressure alongside heterogeneous household capacity/opportunities. No claim of automatic cross-border movement, single-cause attribution or a legal protection category is made.

questions.correctOption: It can reduce information and settlement costs, making the destination more feasible.
questions.independentReview: Matched each supplied network resource to a reduced information/settlement constraint. Kept facilitation distinct from guaranteed success or an exclusive motive; no new destination resources are imported.

questions.correctOption: A political or institutional intervening obstacle to the intended move.
questions.independentReview: Classified the specified entry constraint as a barrier, preserving the distinction between attraction and feasibility. No real-country legal rules, eligibility determination or advice is asserted.

questions.correctOption: Migration can be selective because opportunities and capacity vary among population groups.
questions.independentReview: Used the explicit difference between mover composition and origin composition to identify selectivity. Avoided ecological inference about all older people or deterministic claims about education.

questions.correctOption: Social ties and environmental amenities can be pull factors alongside economic ones.
questions.independentReview: Classified family proximity and preferred climate as social/environmental destination attractions. No medical claim about climate or guarantee of successful relocation is implied.

questions.correctOption: B has the higher departure rate, 10% versus A’s 1%, despite fewer departures.
questions.independentReview: Independently computed100/10000=.01 and10/100=.1. A’s count is larger but B’s normalized rate is ten times higher; neither permits causal attribution.
